title: The King's Three Wise Men
body: Long ago, a king in India asked his three wise men to prove what was more important: clever thinking, pure luck, or a mix of both. To show their answers, the first wise man presented a chessboard to prove that the smartest mind wins. The second brought dice to show how luck rules everything, and the third brought backgammon to show how skill can tame bad luck. The king loved chess the most, calling it the most noble and honorable game.

variants.lucy: Once in ancient India, a king asked his advisors to show him whether clever planning or simple luck guides our lives. One advisor brought rolling dice, another brought a game of mixed chance, but the last one quietly presented a beautiful chessboard. The ruler gazed at the carved pieces and decided that this thoughtful game of pure skill was the most wonderful of all.
variants.luca: Imagine a royal challenge where three thinkers had to prove what rules the world: brainpower, wild luck, or a bit of each! One competitor brought dice for chaotic chance, and another brought a game where skill fights back against bad luck. But the winner brought a chessboard to prove that a sharp mind wins every single battle. The king absolutely loved chess, declaring it the greatest and most respectable game of all!
variants.cn: 从前，在古老的印度，有一位国王问他的三位谋士：到底是聪明的计划，还是单纯的运气，在指引我们的生活？一位谋士带来了骰子，另一位带来了一种又靠运气又靠本事的游戏，最后一位却安安静静地捧出一张漂亮的国际象棋棋盘。国王看着那些精雕细刻的棋子，最后决定：这种全靠动脑的游戏，才是世界上最美妙的游戏。

source.author: Alfonso X (Castilla), ed. Raúl Orellana Calderón
